computed_quantities.name: weight_bytes_per_layer
computed_quantities.derivation: W is 512x512 FP32 = 262144 floats x 4 bytes = 1048576 bytes. Bias is 512 FP32 = 2048 bytes. Total = 1048576 + 2048 = 1050624 bytes.

computed_quantities.name: ceil_weight_bias_MiB_per_layer
computed_quantities.derivation: 1050624 bytes / (1024*1024) = 1.0019 MiB. Ceiling to integer MiB yields 2 MiB per the planner policy.

computed_quantities.name: modeled_memory_budget_per_device
computed_quantities.derivation: Policy dictates 9 MiB minus 1 MiB workspace = 8 MiB modeled budget per device.

computed_quantities.name: max_layers_per_device_by_policy
computed_quantities.derivation: 8 MiB budget / 2 MiB ceil per layer = 4 layers maximum resident per device.

computed_quantities.name: activation_buffer_bytes_per_device
computed_quantities.derivation: Two ping-pong buffers: 2 * B(8) * width(512) * sizeof(float)(4) = 32768 bytes = 32 KiB.

computed_quantities.name: activation_payload_bytes
computed_quantities.derivation: Single buffer transfer: B(8) * width(512) * 4 bytes = 16384 bytes = 16 KiB.

computed_quantities.name: fp32_gemm_multiply_ops_per_layer
computed_quantities.derivation: Batch(8) * M(512) * N(512) * K(512) = 1,073,741,824 individual multiply operations.

computed_quantities.name: fp32_gemm_add_ops_per_layer
computed_quantities.derivation: Batch(8) * M(512) * N(512) * K(512) = 1,073,741,824 individual add operations following multiplies.

computed_quantities.name: fp32_gemm_fma_count_per_layer
computed_quantities.derivation: If hardware fuses multiply+add into FMA, count is B*M*N*K = 1,073,741,824 FMAs. Note: 1 FMA = 1 multiply + 1 add.

computed_quantities.name: residual_add_ops_per_layer
computed_quantities.derivation: Element-wise addition of input x to GEMM output: B(8) * width(512) = 4096 additions.

computed_quantities.name: relu_ops_per_layer
computed_quantities.derivation: Element-wise max(0, val): B(8) * width(512) = 4096 comparisons/assignments.

computed_quantities.name: cold_weight_upload_bytes
computed_quantities.derivation: All 8 layer weights uploaded once before inference begins. No full model replication; split 4 layers to Device A, 4 to Device B.

computed_quantities.name: per_inference_initial_input_upload_bytes
computed_quantities.derivation: Initial input activation for batch 8 uploaded to first device: 8 * 512 * 4 = 16384 bytes.

computed_quantities.name: parity_readback_bytes
computed_quantities.derivation: All 8 layer outputs read back for parity: 8 layers * 16384 bytes/layer = 131072 bytes.

computed_quantities.name: boundary_staged_copy_bytes
computed_quantities.derivation: One inter-device stage boundary: GPUA -> Host -> GPUB transfers exactly one activation payload of 16384 bytes.

computed_quantities.name: boundary_host_copy_count
computed_quantities.derivation: GPUA->Host (readback) and Host->GPUB (upload). Reuses existing parity readback mechanism instead of extra dedicated copy.

latency_equations: T_uninstrumented = T_cold_weights + T_input_H2D + sum_{s=1}^{2} [ sum_{l=1}^{4} (T_kernel_l + T_event_q) + T_ping_pong_swap ] + T_boundary + T_final_readback
T_kernel_l = f(GEMM_ops_l, residual_ops_l, relu_ops_l, device_arch_l) [unknown measured value]
T_event_q = overhead of clEnqueueNDRangeKernel + clFinish/clWaitForEvents per kernel launch
Note: T_readback_A_to_host at boundary can overlap with or reuse the parity readback buffer for layer 4, avoiding double-transfer cost in instrumented mode
assumptions: Weights are resident and uploaded exactly once prior to inference execution; no dynamic weight streaming.
No full model replication across devices; layers 0-3 on Device A, layers 4-7 on Device B.
Exactly one inter-device stage boundary exists between layer 3 and layer 4.
Activation ping-pong uses two pre-allocated buffers per device swapping roles each layer within a stage.
The 8 MiB modeled memory budget is a strict policy cap forcing partitioning, not a reflection of physical VRAM limits.
AMD integrated GPU utilizes host-shared memory architecture; this does not equate to an external dedicated 8GB discrete card.

Default activation payload is 16 KiB (8*512*4 bytes). One payload read from A plus one upload to B equals 16 KiB transferred twice (32 KiB bus traffic), but represents only 16 KiB of unique neural activation state, not 32 KiB of distinct neural data.
Parity instrumentation reads all 8 layer outputs solely for correctness verification and is logically separated from the un-instrumented executor path.
OpenCL buffer allocation reuses existing context memory; it is not assumed to be a fresh VRAM lease from the OS/driver per call.
Serial layer dependencies strictly prevent uniform 4x speedup claims across non-uniform mixed devices.
Four-device hypothetical scaling and 32 GB pooled buffer concepts remain theoretically unproven for this specific topology.
measurement_requirements: Measure per-stage kernel execution times (T_kernel_l) independently on both NVIDIA 5070 Ti and AMD iGPU via OpenCL profiling events.
Measure OpenCL event queue overhead (clEnqueue*, clWait*) separately from kernel execution time.
Characterize H2D and D2H bandwidth and fixed latency for both the PCIe discrete GPU and the system-bus/integrated GPU paths.
Execute CPU reference implementation to establish baseline correctness and timing for parity comparison.
Run warm vs cold start comparisons to isolate initialization/caching effects from steady-state inference.
Verify equal precision (strict FP32) across both devices and CPU reference before accepting parity.
Test execution order variations (Device A first vs Device B first) to detect order-dependent state bugs.
Establish two-GPU partitioned baseline vs one-GPU full-model baseline to quantify partitioning overhead.
Disable all parity instrumentation when measuring performance bounds; only benchmark after correctness is formally accepted.
Validate that actual OpenCL clCreateBuffer calls do not trigger unexpected physical memory reallocation during the ping-pong loop.
forbidden_claims: Do not claim empirical bandwidth numbers, TFLOPS, or throughput without direct measurement on the specific hardware configuration.
Do not claim LLM-derived or approximate hardware performance specifications as theoretical bounds.
Do not claim the 8 MiB policy cap proves physical VRAM capacity limits of either device.
Do not claim AMD integrated host-shared memory functions equivalently to a discrete 8GB dedicated VRAM pool.
Do not promise uniform 4x speedup from non-uniform devices with serial layer dependencies.
Do not claim four-device hypothetical larger workloads or 32 GB pooled buffers are proven or achievable by this derivation.
Do not claim 32 KiB of neural activation state exists at the boundary; 16 KiB read + 16 KiB write is 16 KiB of unique activation data moved twice.
Do not assume OpenCL buffer creation constitutes a fresh VRAM lease rather than a mapped handle to pre-allocated ping-pong memory.
Do not conflate parity-instrumented execution latency with un-instrumented production inference latency.
Do not claim direct API calls create child processes or execute unauthorized workers outside the specified single-host OpenCL context.
